python3 -c "
import cv2
import numpy as np
import math

# Let's inspect obs_0017:
# pose: x=-0.25, y=0.9330, heading=90.0
# The cabinet wood doors are on the left:
img17 = cv2.imread('/work/observations/obs_0017.png')
# find wood doors in obs_0017:
mask_doors = (img17[:, :, 0] > 90) & (img17[:, :, 0] < 150) & (img17[:, :, 1] > 100) & (img17[:, :, 1] < 160) & (img17[:, :, 2] > 110) & (img17[:, :, 2] < 180)
# Look at columns 0 to 150, rows 300 to 450
ys, xs = np.where(mask_doors)
print('obs_0017 doors cols:', xs.min(), xs.max(), 'rows:', ys.min(), ys.max())

# Bottom edge of the wood doors in obs_0017:
# For each column from xs.min() to xs.max(), find max y:
bottom_ys = [np.where(mask_doors[:, c])[0].max() for c in range(xs.min(), xs.max()+1) if np.any(mask_doors[:, c])]
print('Bottom rows across doors in obs_0017:', min(bottom_ys), max(bottom_ys))
print('Rightmost edge of doors in obs_0017:', xs.max(), 'at row', np.where(mask_doors[:, xs.max()])[0].max())
print('Leftmost edge of doors in obs_0017:', xs.min(), 'at row', np.where(mask_doors[:, xs.min()])[0].max())
"
